text:
jin: Kicking off a small canary for hera13b (int4). Noticed a couple of OOMs and 99p tail when concurrent batches >3 during smoke runs.
ashwin: Can you paste the exact launch flags (batch_max, timeout, prefetch, max_new_tokens, eviction)?
maria: FYI mixed short/long prompts historically cause KV churn and slab fragmentation.
jin: Launch flags:
```
model: hera13b-int4
batch_max: 8
batch_timeout_ms: 22
prefetch: true
max_new_tokens_default: 240
soft_eviction: false
kv_prefetch_slots: 30
```
sam: prefetch + big max_new is suspect. Suggest try prefetch=false and drop max_new to 120, also lower batch_soft_limit to 15ms.
ajay (ml-eval-bot): queued matrix: batch 1,2,4; max_new 64,120,240; prefetch on/off.
jin: Quick results: prefetch=true batch=4 max_new=240 -> 3 OOMs, 99p~820ms. prefetch=false batch=4 max_new=240 -> 1 OOM, 99p~600ms. prefetch=false batch=2 max_new=120 -> 0 OOMs, 99p~240ms.
maria: consistent with fragmentation hypothesis: long prompts (~700 tokens) create big KV allocations that, when prefetched, leave gaps and increase free fragment count.
nashwin: Check gen_window and microbatching? Kernel stalls + continuous batching can add tail.
jin: gen_window=12, microbatching off in this config.
sam: Proposed safe defaults for canary: batch_max=4, batch_timeout_ms=15, prefetch=false, max_new_tokens_default=120, soft_eviction=true. Apply to pool-hera-canary.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: hera13b-int4 @ pool-hera-canary (8 instances).
ajay (ml-eval-bot): running synthetic traffic (QPS 110), mix 30% long / 70% short, collecting traces.
jin: After 40m: 0 OOMs, 99p=250-290ms, occasional 320ms spikes.
maria: Did ablation toggling soft_eviction=false?
ajay (ml-eval-bot): ablation: soft_eviction=false -> 2 OOMs in 30m. Re-enabled soft_eviction.
sam: Good. Please add a telemetry metric for repeated large-kv allocs per session (alert if >3 in 2s) and an automatic rollback threshold.
jin: Filed INFRA-8811 for telemetry + rollback.
maria: Also add a note to model-onboard checklist: "for mixed prompt-length models, start with prefetch=false and conservative max_new_tokens until mem-frag validated".
nashwin: Any QoE impact from lowering max_new? Run QA on canonical prompts.
ajay (ml-eval-bot): QA run: no significant degradation on standard evals (perplexity/BLEU/ROUGE deltas <0.6%); edge-case long-tail tests OK.
jin: TL;DR: root cause = prefetch + large max_new_tokens + higher concurrent batches -> KV fragmentation -> sporadic OOMs and tail. Mitigation = conservative defaults (batch_timeout 15ms, prefetch=false, max_new_tokens_default=120, soft_eviction=true), add telemetry + gradual rollout. Plan: 24h clean canary then 50% pool rollout.
sam: :thumbsup: roll when 24h clean and infra alerts green.
jin: Thanks all — documenting in onboarding checklist and closing thread. :rocket:
